Why you should never hide your router in a closet: 5 steps to speed up your slow Wi-Fi

Mesh is ok, but remember that all mesh is not equal. They are usually not access points but repeaters, meaning the data has to go from your device to the repeater then to the main router, all wirelessly. Many are half-duplex, meaning latency is much higher than a direct connection to the main router. You will be much better off if you can install access points that are connected to your main router via ethernet. And in many cases this can be much cheaper, if a little more complicated. A good router can be around $100 and good access points (like an AP AC-Lite) are under $100. Cut off the main routers WIFI and put the AP on the ceiling (or put one AP at one end of the house and the router at the other). Many look pretty much like a smoke detector or similar device and blend right in.
